title: Error Tracking for R Applications via GlitchTip and Sentry
text: gt_capture() framework-agnostic. Shiny, use directly inside renderPlot(), observeEvent(), reactive context.
code: library(shiny) library(glitchtipr)  gt <- gt_connect()  server <- function(input, output, session) {   # In render functions, Shiny catches the re-raised error and displays it   # in the output — no extra handling needed.   output$plot <- renderPlot({     gt_capture(gt, {       x <- faithful[, 2]       bins <- seq(min(x), max(x), length.out = input$bins + 1)       hist(x, breaks = bins, col = "darkgray", border = "white")     })   })    # In observers, wrap with tryCatch to prevent the session from crashing.   # gt_capture() has already reported the error before it propagates.   observeEvent(input$crash, {     tryCatch(       gt_capture(gt, {         stop("Something went wrong.")       }),       error = function(e) invisible(NULL)     )   }) }

title: Error Tracking for R Applications via GlitchTip and Sentry
text: Errors propagate — gt_capture() uses withCallingHandlers(), tryCatch(). Errors reported always re-raised. plumber2 Shiny render functions handled automatically. Shiny observers, wrap tryCatch() gt_capture() prevent session crashing. Silent unconfigured — DSN means connection, means gt_capture() pure -op. errors, overhead development. Minimal surface — two functions: gt_connect() gt_capture(). One plumber2 tag: @capture. ’s entire API. Self-hostable — built GlitchTip (open source, Sentry-compatible) works platform implements Sentry store API. Context-aware — report includes endpoint, query string, sanitised headers (Authorization Cookie stripped automatically).
